item.title: Beats, bars and belonging at ACE
item.description: Aspiration Creation Elevation (ACE) offers creative support and guidance to young people. With them, Adam explores the complex realities young people face today - and reflects on his own journey along the way The post Beats, bars and belonging at ACE appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Play, a risky business: A tour of Bristol’s Adventure Playgrounds
item.description: The Cable's community organiser explores the history and enduring spirit of the city's Adventure Playgrounds, where children are trusted, challenged and free to play The post Play, a risky business: A tour of Bristol’s Adventure Playgrounds appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Surveillance isn’t safeguarding: Think Family and the fight for transparency
item.description: Bristol City Council says its mass data gathering tool is designed to protect, not profile the 55,000 families it monitors. But is it pushing school children into the criminal justice system? The post Surveillance isn’t safeguarding: Think Family and the fight for transparency appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Listen: Bristol Unpacked with police and crime commissioner Clare Moody on fixing force culture, and the government axing her role
item.description: Just 18 months into her term, the Labour politician in charge of police scrutiny in Avon and Somerset has, along with peers across the country, been told she represents a 'failed experiment' that will end in 2028. Neil asks Clare Moody how that feels, and what she aims to achieve while still in office. The post Listen: Bristol Unpacked with police and crime commissioner Clare Moody on fixing force culture, and the government axing her role appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Hurt people, hurt people: The hidden lives of children behind bars
item.description: At 10 years old, England and Wales has one of the lowest ages of criminal responsibility in the world. Here we offer a glimpse into child incarceration, the school to prison pipeline and stalling youth justice system reforms. Starting here, on the outskirts of Bristol... The post Hurt people, hurt people: The hidden lives of children behind bars appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: The Sudanese Bristolians using art to cope with displacement
item.description: In the shadow of a brutal civil war, a collective of Sudanese women in Bristol are bonding over coffee and creativity The post The Sudanese Bristolians using art to cope with displacement appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Listen: Bristol Unpacked with Green councillor Ani Townsend on art, inequality and the case for a universal basic income
item.description: Should the state give people free money? This week Ani and Neil discuss how a universal basic income would work, why supporting the arts is a class issue, and whether ‘eco-populist’ Green leader Zack Polanski can take on the traditional parties – and Reform. The post Listen: Bristol Unpacked with Green councillor Ani Townsend on art, inequality and the case for a universal basic income appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.description: A jury has refused to convict the six activists, who broke into and disrupted operations at an Israeli arms firm in Filton, after a high-profile and politically-charged trial The post Palestine Action’s ‘Filton 6’ cleared in ‘huge victory for moral courage in face of political pressure’ appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Bristol’s Kurdish community rallies for Rojava
item.description: As attacks intensify in northern Syria, Kurdish Bristolians Tara and Tanya speak to the Cable about betrayal, resistance and why the women-led revolution must be defended The post Bristol’s Kurdish community rallies for Rojava appeared first on The Bristol Cable.
